translations.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

The Lord handed it over to him, along with Jehoiakim king of Judah and the vessels of the Lord’s house. He brought some of the vessels of the Lord’s house to the land of Shinar, to the temple of his idol, and put the vessels in his idol’s treasury.
The king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the Israelites, including some from the royal family and the nobility:

young men without any physical defect, handsome in appearance, skilled in wisdom, knowledgeable and discerning, and physically able to serve in the king’s palace. They were to be taught the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
The king assigned them a daily portion of the king’s rich food and of the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years and then enter the king’s service.
Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from the people of Judah.
The chief eunuch gave them names: he called Daniel Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
Daniel resolved not to eat the king’s rich food or drink the wine he drank, and he asked the chief of the eunuchs not to make him eat it.
God granted Daniel favor and compassion in the eyes of the chief of the eunuchs.

The chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who has prescribed your food and drink. If he sees that your faces look worse than those of the other young men your age, the king will cut off my head.”
Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Test your servants for ten days, and let us be given vegetables to eat and water to drink.
“Compare our appearance with the appearance of the young men who eat the king’s rich food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
He agreed to their request and tested them for ten days.
After ten days, he saw that their faces looked better and their bodies were better nourished than those of all the young men who ate the king’s rich food.
The steward would take away their allotted food and the wine they were to drink, and give them vegetables to eat and water to drink.
God gave these four young men knowledge and understanding in all literature and wisdom, and Daniel understood all visions and dreams.
When the period the king had prescribed was over, the chief of the eunuchs brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke with them, and among them all he found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his kingdom.
Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had a dream. His spirit was troubled, and sleep came over him.
The king ordered the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans to be summoned to tell the king his dream. They came and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled because I want to understand the dream.”
The Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic, saying, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
The king answered the Chaldeans, “What I have said is firm: unless you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will be cut limb from limb, and your houses will be plundered.
But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will receive gifts, wealth, and great honor from me. Just tell me the dream and its meaning.”
They answered him again, saying, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
The king answered, “I know for certain that you are asking for time because you see that my decision is firm.

If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one sentence for you. You have agreed to speak lies and empty words before me until the time passes. But tell me the dream, so that I may know that you can also tell me its interpretation.”
The Chaldeans answered the king, “There is no one on earth who can reveal what the king asks. No great and powerful king has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
What the king asks is difficult, and no one can reveal it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortal human beings.”
Then the king became extremely angry, and in great fury he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed.
The decree went out, and the wise men were being killed. They also sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.
Then Daniel considered the matter, took counsel, and spoke to Arioch, the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
“Why has such a harsh decree gone out from the king?” Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
Daniel asked the king to give him time, so that he could make the interpretation known to the king.
Then Daniel went home and explained this matter to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
so that they would seek mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision at night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel said, “May the name of the Lord be blessed forever and ever, for wisdom and might belong to him.
He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and establishes kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what is in the darkness, and light is with him.
I thank and praise you, God of my ancestors, because you have given me wisdom and might. Now you have made known to me what we asked of you; you have made the king’s matter known to me.”

At that very hour Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had ordered to kill the wise men of Babylon. He went and said to him, “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Instead, bring me before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation.”
Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the captives from Judah who will make the interpretation known to the king.”
The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Can you tell me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?”
Daniel answered before the king, “Neither wise men, magi, magicians, nor enchanters can reveal to the king the mystery that the king asks about.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who will make known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days. This is your dream and the vision in your mind as you lay on your bed:
You, O king, began to think about what would happen in the future, and the revealer of mysteries made known to you what would happen.

As for me, this mystery was not revealed to me because I have more wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that the interpretation might be made known to the king and you might understand what you were thinking in your heart.
You, O king, were looking, and there before you stood a great statue, exceedingly bright and terrifying in appearance.
Its head was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, and its belly and thighs of bronze.
Its legs were iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly clay.
You saw a stone cut out without hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them completely.

Then the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold were all crushed together and became like chaff from a summer threshing floor. A strong wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This is the dream, and he told its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings. The Most High God has given you a mighty kingdom and honor.
Wherever human beings live, he has given them into your hands, along with the birds of the sky and the wild animals, and has made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours. Then another, a third kingdom, which is bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
A fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. Just as iron breaks and crushes everything, so it too will crush and subdue everything.
As for the feet and toes you saw, partly potter’s clay and partly iron, the kingdom will be divided. But some of the firmness of iron will remain in it, just as you saw iron mixed with earthen clay.
As for the toes of the feet that you saw, partly iron and partly clay, part of the kingdom will be strong and part will be broken.
As you saw iron mixed with earthen clay, so they will mingle through human offspring, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed. The kingdom will not be left to another people. Instead, it will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.

Just as you saw a stone cut out of the mountain without hands, which crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold, the great God has made known to you what will happen in the last days. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and worshiped Daniel, and ordered incense and offerings to be presented to him.
The king answered Daniel, saying, “Truly, your God is the God of gods, the Lord of kings, and the revealer of mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many gifts. He made him ruler over the whole land of Babylon and appointed him chief over all the military commanders and all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel petitioned the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon. Daniel remained at the king’s gate.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the land of Babylon.

King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the military commanders, nobles, governors, [?], [?], [?], magistrates, and all the provincial authorities, to come to the festival for the new statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then all the military commanders, nobles, governors, [?], [?], [?], magistrates, and all the provincial authorities assembled and came to the festival for the new statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. They stood before the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
The herald called out loudly, saying, “You are commanded, peoples, nations, and languages:
As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire.”

As soon as the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the gold statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that very time, some Chaldean men came forward and brought accusations against the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, live forever!
You, O king, commanded that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music should fall down and worship the gold statue you set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship is to be thrown into the blazing furnace.

There are certain Jewish men here whom you appointed over the affairs of the city of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men have disregarded you, O king. They do not serve your god or worship the gold statue you set up.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought in. They brought them before the king.
King Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my god or worship the gold statue I set up?

Now, if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the statue I made. But if you do not worship, you will immediately be thrown into the blazing furnace. And who is your god, that he should rescue you from my hands?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered King Nebuchadnezzar, “We have no need to give you an answer concerning this matter.
For our God, whom we serve, has the power to rescue us from the blazing furnace, and he will deliver us from your hands, O king.
But know, O king, that we do not serve your god or worship the gold statue you set up.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and his expression changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than it was usually heated.
He ordered men of great strength to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
Then those men bound them in their trousers, tunics, clothes, and hats, and threw them into the blazing furnace.
Because the king’s command was urgent and the furnace was heated exceedingly hot, the flame of the blazing fire killed the men who had accused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
And those three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the middle of the blazing furnace.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose in great fear. He said to his officials, “Did we not throw three men, bound, into the blazing furnace?” They answered the king, “Yes, indeed, O king.”
The king said, “Look! I see men unbound and walking in the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

Then King Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the blazing furnace and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the furnace.

All the peoples, army commanders, governors, rulers, and the king’s officials gathered together. They saw that the fire had had no power over these men’s bodies: the hair of their heads was not singed, their trousers were not burned, and not even the smell of fire had touched them.

King Nebuchadnezzar said, “Blessed is the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and rescued his servants! They trusted in him, rejected the king’s command, and gave up their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.

Therefore I command that anyone of any people, nation, or language who blasphemes against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be cut limb from limb, and their houses shall be plundered, because there is no other god who can deliver like this.”
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the region of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages living throughout the earth: “May your peace increase!
I thought it good to make known the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed.
How great are his signs, and how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion endures from generation to generation.”
Do not give us up completely, for your name’s sake, and do not annul your covenant.
Do not withdraw your mercy and kindness from us, for the sake of Abraham your friend, Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one.
You promised them that you would multiply their descendants like the stars in heaven and like the sand on the seashore.
For now, Lord, we have been brought lower than all the nations, and today we are scattered throughout the earth because of our offenses and sins.
At this time there is no chief or ruler, no prophet or leader, no altar, sacrifices, or offerings, and no place where we can offer incense or a sacrifice and find favor and mercy.
But with a broken heart and a humble spirit, here we have been offered up to be burned in the fire.
So, as we pray, may the offering of ourselves today be greater than bulls, rams, and many fat lambs. May your servants not be put to shame, for those who trust in you are not put to shame.
Even now we follow you wholeheartedly. We have feared you, and we seek your face.
Lord, do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to your abundant kindness and your great mercy.
Deliver us according to your many wonders, and bring glory to your name, Lord, for the sake of your great name.
May all who speak evil against your servants be put to shame. May they be put to shame despite all their might, and may their strength desert them.
May they know that you alone are the one God, and that you are praised in all your works.
Those who were heating the fiery furnace did not stop. They kept throwing naphtha, pitch, sulfur, reeds, and vine shoots into it.
The flame of the fire roared and rose forty-nine cubits above the furnace.
The fire burned and destroyed everyone it found around the furnace, both Chaldeans and accusers.
But the angel of dew went down with Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael into the fiery furnace and drove the flame of fire out of the furnace.
He made the inside of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze. The fire did not come near them at all, nor did it hurt or distress them.
Then all three, with one voice, praised and blessed God from inside the fiery furnace, saying:
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our ancestors. You are praised and exalted forever. Blessed is your holy and glorious name. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in your holy temple. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you who see the depths and sit enthroned upon the cherubim. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you on your royal throne. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the expanse of heaven. You are praised and exalted forever.
All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
All you angels of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
You heavens of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
You waters above the heavens, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever. All you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s hosts. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, sun and moon. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, stars in heaven. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, rain and dew. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, waters and winds. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fire and heat. Praise him and exalt him forever. Bless the Lord, all the souls of the righteous. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, frost and heat. Praise him and exalt him forever. Bless the Lord, summer and winter. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, snow and ice. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, nights and days. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, light and darkness. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, lightning and clouds. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, earth. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, mountains and hills. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the vegetation of the earth. Praise him and exalt him forever. Bless the Lord, everything that grows on the earth. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fountains and all springs. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, seas and rivers. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fish and everything that moves in the waters. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all birds of the sky. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all wild animals and livestock. Praise him and exalt him forever. Bless the Lord, everything that moves on the earth. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all human beings. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all who belong to the house of Israel. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s priests. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s servants. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the souls and spirits of the righteous. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, you who are blameless and humble in heart. Praise him and exalt him forever.

Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael. Praise him and exalt him forever, because he has saved us from death, preserved our lives from the power of Sheol, rescued us from the burning flame, and brought us out of the midst of the fire.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever. Praise him and exalt him forever.
All you who fear God, bless the God of gods. Praise him and exalt him forever. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and at rest in my palace.
I saw a dream and was disturbed, and the visions in my head troubled me.
I ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be brought before me, so that they could tell me the interpretation of the dream.
The magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and sorcerers came before me. I told them the dream, but they did not make its interpretation known to me.
At last Daniel came before me, whose name was Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and in whom was the spirit of the holy gods. I told him the dream:

Belteshazzar, chief of the wise men, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery is hidden from you. In the vision of my dream I see a vision in my head; tell me its interpretation.
As I watched on my bed, there was a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.
The tree grew tall and strong, and its height reached heaven. It was visible to all the ends of the earth.

Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit was abundant, and it had food for all living creatures. All the wild animals lived beneath it, all the birds of the sky nested in its branches, and every living creature was fed from it.
As I watched in the visions in my head while on my bed, there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
He called out loudly and said, 'Cut down the tree, lop off its branches, strip off its leaves, and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from beneath it and the birds of the sky from its branches.

But leave its stump and roots in the earth, bound with iron and bronze, among the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his dwelling be with the wild animals among the grass of the earth.
Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let an animal's mind be given to him. Let seven periods of time pass over him.

This sentence is by the watcher's command, and this demand is by the holy one's word, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity. He gives it to whomever he wishes and sets the lowliest of people over it.'

This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can make it known to me. But you, Daniel, can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stunned for about an hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king spoke and said, 'Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation trouble you.' Daniel answered, 'My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
The tree that you saw, which grew large and strong, whose height reached heaven, and which was visible to all the ends of the earth—

its leaves were beautiful, its fruit was abundant, and it had food for all living creatures. All the wild animals lived beneath it, all the birds of the sky nested in its branches, and every living creature was fed from it.
It is you, O king, who have become strong and great. You have grown and reached heaven, and your dominion extends to all the ends of the earth.

The king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven, calling out loudly and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave its stump and roots in the earth, bound with iron and bronze, among the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his dwelling be with the wild animals among the grass of the earth. Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let an animal's mind be given to him until seven periods of time pass over him.'
This is the interpretation, O king: the decree of the Most High has come upon my lord the king.

You will be driven away from people, and your dwelling will be with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like an ox, and you will be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity, gives it to whomever he wishes, and sets the lowliest of people over it.
And as for the command to leave the stump and roots of the tree, your kingdom will remain yours once you acknowledge that authority comes from heaven.
Therefore, may my advice be acceptable to you: redeem your sins through charitable giving, and your wrongdoing through mercy toward the weak, until your offenses are removed from you.
All these things happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
After twelve months, King Nebuchadnezzar was walking on the roof of his royal palace in Babylon.
He spoke and said, “Is this not great Babylon, which I built as the home of my kingdom, for my mighty dominion and my honor?”
While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven: “To you it is declared, King Nebuchadnezzar: your kingdom has passed from you.

You will be driven away from human society, and your dwelling will be with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like an ox and drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you, until you acknowledge that God Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity, gives it to whomever he wishes, and sets the lowliest of people over it.”

At that very moment, the declaration was fulfilled against King Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from human society, ate grass like an ox, and was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like an eagle’s feathers and his nails like a bird’s claws.

When those days were over, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me. I blessed the Most High and praised and honored the one who lives forever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion and whose kingdom endures from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are regarded as nothing before him. He does whatever he wishes among the armies of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth. No one can restrain his hand or say to him, “What are you doing?”
At that time my understanding returned to me. My nobles and military commanders sought me out, and I was restored to my kingdom, and still greater majesty was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of heaven, whose deeds are all true and whose ways are just, and who is able to humble those who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar held a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in front of the thousand.

Under the influence of his wine, Belshazzar ordered the gold and silver vessels that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem to be brought, so that the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines could drink from them.
Then they brought the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
At that very moment, the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote opposite the lamp on the plaster of the wall in the king’s palace. The king saw the hand as it wrote.
Then the king’s face changed color, his thoughts troubled him, the joints of his hips loosened, and his knees knocked against each other.

The king shouted loudly for the enchanters, Chaldeans, magicians, and wise men to be brought in. The king addressed the wise men of Babylon and said, “Whoever reads this writing and explains its interpretation to me will be clothed in purple, have a gold chain around his neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”
Then the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make its interpretation known to the king.
Then King Belshazzar became greatly troubled, his face changed color, and his nobles were bewildered.

Because of the words of the king and his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. She addressed the king and said, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you or your face change color.

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In your father's days, enlightenment, understanding, and great wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans.

For an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him: Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, interprets dreams, explains riddles, and solves difficult problems. Now let Daniel be summoned, and he will explain the interpretation.”
Then Daniel came before the king. The king addressed Daniel and said, “Are you Daniel, one of the captives of Judah whom my father the king brought from Judah?
I have heard about you, that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and that illumination, understanding, and extraordinary wisdom have been found in you.
The magicians were brought before me to read this writing and show me its interpretation, but they could not make its meaning known to me.

But I have heard about you that you can explain interpretations and solve difficult problems. If you can read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed in purple, with a gold chain around your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom.
Then Daniel answered the king, saying, “Keep your gifts for yourself, and give the honors of your house to others. Nevertheless, I will read the writing for the king and show him its interpretation.
As for you, O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingship, greatness, honor, and glory.

Because of the greatness he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled before him and feared him. He killed whomever he wished and kept alive whomever he wished; he raised up whomever he wished and brought low whomever he wished.
But when his heart became proud and his spirit grew stubborn with arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne, and his honor was taken away from him.

He was driven away from human beings, and his mind became like that of wild animals. He lived with the wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew like an eagle’s feathers and his nails like a bird’s claws, until he learned that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity, gives it to whomever he wishes, and sets the lowliest of people over it.
But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.

You have raised yourself up against the Lord of heaven. The vessels of his house were brought before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which neither see nor hear nor know. But the God who holds your breath in his hands, and to whom all your ways belong, you have neither praised nor honored.
Then the hand was sent from his presence,
and it inscribed this writing. This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the matter: Mene—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel—you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.
PERES: Your kingdom is divided and given to Media and Persia.”
Then King Belshazzar gave the order, and they clothed Daniel in purple, put a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed that he was to rule as third in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
Darius the Mede received the kingdom when he was about sixty-two years old.
Darius decided to appoint 120 military commanders throughout his kingdom.
Over them were three administrators, one of whom was Daniel. These military commanders were to give accounts to them so that the king would suffer no loss.
Then Daniel distinguished himself above all of them because an exceptional spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over his whole kingdom.

Then the officials and military commanders tried to find grounds for accusing Daniel concerning the affairs of the kingdom. But they could find no fault or grounds for accusation against him, because he was faithful to his God, and they found no wrongdoing or fault in him.
Those men said, “We will find no grounds for a charge against this Daniel unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”
Then the administrators and military commanders approached the king and said to him, “King Darius, live forever!

All the administrators of the kingdom, the nobles, the military commanders, and the governors have agreed that the king should establish a decree and enforce a prohibition: whoever makes a petition to any god or human being other than you, O king, for thirty days is to be thrown into the lions’ den.
Now, O king, issue this command and put it in writing, so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of Media and Persia, and cannot be altered.”
Then King Darius signed the document and issued the command.

When Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house. The windows of his upstairs room were open toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he knelt on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.
Then those men kept watch and found Daniel making petitions and pleading before his God.

Then they approached and said before the king, “O king, live forever! Did you not issue and sign a decree that anyone who makes a request of any god or human being within thirty days, except of you, O king, should be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king answered, “The matter is established according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”
Then they answered and said before the king, “Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, has paid no attention to you or to the decree you issued, and he makes his petition three times.”
When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed and set his mind on rescuing Daniel. Until sunset he kept striving to rescue him.
Then those men pressed the king and said to him, “Know, O king, that the Medes and Persians have a law that no decree or statute established by the king may be changed.”
Then the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “Your God, whom you serve continually, will save you.”
They brought a stone and placed it over the mouth of the den. The king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No food was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
Then, in the morning, the king rose in haste and went quickly to the lions’ den.

As he approached the den, he called out to Daniel in a loud voice. The king said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?”
Then Daniel spoke to the king and said, “O king, live forever!
My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. And I have done no wrong against you either, O king.”
Then the king was greatly pleased and ordered Daniel to be brought up from the den. They brought Daniel up from the den, and no injury was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

The king said, “Bring those men who accused Daniel and throw them into the lions’ den, along with their wives and children.” They threw them into the den, and before they reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages dwelling throughout the earth: “May your peace increase!

I issue a decree that throughout the dominion of my kingdom people must tremble and fear before Daniel's God. For he is the living God and endures forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his dominion lasts to the end.
He redeems, saves, and rescues, and performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He saved Daniel from the lions.”
Daniel rose to greatness during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar, king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions in his mind as he lay on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and related the main points.
Daniel said, “I was watching in a vision of the night, and there were the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea.
Four great beasts came up from the sea, each different from the others.

The first was like a lion and had an eagle’s wings. I watched as its wings were plucked off. It was lifted up from the ground and stood on its feet like a human being, and a human heart was given to it.
The second beast resembled a wolf. It stood up on one side and had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, ‘Get up and eat much flesh!’
After this I saw another beast, like a leopard, with four bird’s wings on its back. This beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.

After this I saw in the vision of the night a fourth beast, terrifying, powerful, and exceedingly strong. It had large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, and trampled with its feet whatever remained. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
I was studying its horns, and a little horn came up among them. Three of the earlier horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking boastfully.

I watched as thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head was like pure wool. His throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.
A river of fire flowed and came out from before him. A thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The Judge sat down, and the books were opened.
I watched as that beast was killed, its body was destroyed, and it was handed over to be burned with fire.
The rest of the beasts were stripped of their authority, but an extension of life was given to them for a season and a time.
I watched as someone like a son of man came on the clouds of heaven. He reached the Ancient of Days, and they brought him before him.

He gave him authority, kingship, and honor, so that all peoples, nations, and languages would serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
My spirit was distressed—I, Daniel, was in my bed—and the visions in my head troubled me.
I approached one of the attendants and questioned him about the truth of all these things. He told me the truth and made their meaning known to me.
He said to me, “These four great beasts that you saw are four kings who will arise from the earth.
But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever, for ever and ever.”

Then I wanted to inquire about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others and exceedingly terrifying. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze. It devoured and crushed, and whatever remained it trampled with its feet.

I also wanted to inquire about the ten horns on its head and about the other horn that came up among them, before which three fell. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking boastfully, and its appearance was greater than that of its companions.
I watched as that horn made war against the holy ones and overpowered them,
until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment in favor of the holy ones of the Most High. The time arrived, and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
He said this to me: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth. It will surpass the other kingdoms and devour the whole earth, trampling it and crushing it.
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise from the kingdom, and another will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones and bring down three kings.

He will speak against the Most High and oppress the holy ones of the Most High. He will intend to change the appointed times and laws, and they will be handed over to him for a time, times, and half a time.
The Judge sat down, and they took his authority away from him, to destroy and completely put an end to it.
For kingship, authority, greatness, and the kingdom beneath heaven were given to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all authorities will serve and obey him.”
Here the account ends. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my appearance changed, but I kept the matter in my heart.
In the third year of King Belshazzar’s reign, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the first vision that had appeared to me.
I saw in my dream that I was in Susa, the citadel in the province of Elam. I saw in my dream that I was standing at the Ulai Gate.
I looked up and saw a ram standing in front of the gate. It had horns, and its horns were tall. One was taller than the other, and the taller one grew up last.
I saw the ram charging westward, northward, and southward. No beast could stand before it, and no one could escape its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
While I was considering this, a male goat came from the west across the surface of the whole earth without touching the ground. The goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
It came up to the ram with the horns, which I had seen standing in front of the gate, and rushed at it furiously.

It reached the ram, became furious with it, struck it, and broke both its horns. The ram had no strength to stand against it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled it, and no one could rescue the ram from the goat's power.
The goat grew very great, but when it became strong, its great horn was broken. Four conspicuous horns arose in its place, toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of them came a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the east.
It grew as far as the armies of heaven, cast some of the armies and some of the stars down to the earth, and trampled them.
It reached as far as the commanders of the armies, took the continual offering away from him, and demolished the established place of his sanctuary.
An army was given authority over the regular offering because of sins. The sanctuary was thrown to the ground, and it advanced and prospered.

I heard one holy one speaking, and another holy one said to a certain one who was speaking, “How long will the vision concerning the continual offering, wrongdoing, and destruction last? How long will the sanctuary be handed over and the army be trampled?”
He said to him, “Until two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then righteousness will prevail.”
When I, Daniel, saw the vision, I sought to understand it. And there before me stood someone with the appearance of a man.
I heard a human voice from between the banks of the Ulai, calling out and saying, “Gabriel, make this man understand this vision.”
He came to where I was standing. When he came, I was afraid and fell on my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, that this vision concerns the time of the end.”
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a stupor with my face to the ground. He touched me and made me stand upright.
He said to me, “Look, I am showing you what will happen at the end of the wrath, at the time of the end.
The ram you saw, which had horns, is the king of Media and Persia.
The goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for its being broken and four arising in its place, four kings will arise from the nation, but not by their own strength.
At the end of their reign, when sins have reached their full measure, a fierce-faced king who understands riddles will arise.
His power will be great, but not through his own strength. He will cause astonishing destruction, succeed, and advance. He will destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.

Through his cunning, deceit will succeed in his hands. His heart will become proud, and he will destroy many while they are at ease. He will rise against the ruler of rulers, but he will be broken by the grasp of a hand.
The vision of the morning and evening that was spoken is true. But you, Daniel, conceal this vision, because it concerns many days to come.”
I, Daniel, trembled and was troubled for days. Then I got up and attended to the king's business. I was astonished by the vision, and no one understood it.
In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of Median descent, who became king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, examined the book concerning the number of years. I saw that the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah the prophet concerned the completion of seventy years of Jerusalem's desolation.
I lifted my face before the LORD God to seek him with prayer and supplication, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
I prayed before the LORD my God, confessed, and said, “Please, LORD, great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and shows faithful kindness to those who love him and keep his commandments,
We have sinned, done wrong, acted wickedly, rebelled, and turned aside from your commandments and your judgments.
we have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our nobles, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but shame belongs to us, as it does today—to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, both near and far, in all the lands where you scattered them because of the wrongdoing they committed against you.
Lord, shame belongs to us, to our kings, our leaders, and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
Mercy and forgiveness of sins belong to the Lord God, though we have rebelled against him.
We have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God by following his law, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.

All Israel has transgressed your law and turned aside, refusing to obey your voice. You have brought upon them the curses and oaths written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, because we have sinned before him.

He has fulfilled the words he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing upon us a great disaster. Nothing like what happened in Jerusalem has ever happened anywhere under heaven.
As it is written in the law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us. Yet we have not prayed before the Lord our God that we might turn from our wrongdoing and understand your faithfulness.
The Lord stirred up disaster and brought it upon us, because the Lord our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done, but we have not obeyed his voice.
And now, Lord our God, you brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself that endures to this day. We have sinned and acted wickedly.

Lord, in keeping with all the righteous deeds you have done for us, let your anger and wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem and from your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the wrongdoing of our ancestors, your people have been scattered everywhere, and Jerusalem has become an object of scorn to all the nations.
Now, God, listen to your servant’s prayer and to our pleas, and let your face shine upon your ruined sanctuary, for the sake of your name, Lord.

My God, incline your ear and hear; open your eyes and see our ruins, our desolate places, and the city that bears your name. For we do not rely on our righteousness when we pray before you, but on your great mercy.
Lord, listen! Lord, have mercy! Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for the sake of your name, my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.
While I was praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and presenting my plea before the Lord God concerning the holy mountain of my God,
while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision earlier, came flying and soaring from heaven and approached me at the time of the evening offering.
He came and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have now come out to teach you to understand.
At the beginning of your prayer, a message went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are greatly loved. Consider the message and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks will be laid upon your people and your holy city, to bring transgressions to an end, to finish sins, to forgive wrongdoing, to bring everlasting righteousness, to fulfill the vision and the prophets, and to anoint the Holy of Holies.

Know and understand: from the issuing of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the coming of an anointed king, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. He will return and rebuild Jerusalem, its streets and its squares, until the end of the time.

After the sixty-two weeks, the anointed one will be killed and will have nothing. The holy city will be destroyed along with the king who is coming. Its end will come with a flood, and until the end of the war there will be decreed devastation.

He will strengthen a covenant with many for one week, and for half a week he will put an end to sacrifice and offerings. On the wings of abomination will be destruction, until the full measure of what has been decreed comes to rest upon the destroyer.

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was named Belteshazzar. The message was true, and the message was understood with great power, and he understood it through the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
I ate no desirable food, neither meat nor wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three full weeks were over.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, the Euphrates.
I raised my eyes and looked, and there was a man dressed in splendid clothes, with his waist girded in glorious splendor.

His appearance was extraordinary and beyond comparison. His face looked like lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and shoulders were like gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words was like the sound of many armies.
I, Daniel, alone saw this vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but great terror fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
I alone was left, and I saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; my whole being was overwhelmed, and I had no strength.
When I heard the sound of his words, I fell face down on the ground.
Then a hand touched me and raised me onto my knees and the palms of my hands.
He said to me, “Rise, Daniel, greatly beloved man. Understand the message I am speaking to you, and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you.” As he spoke these words to me, I stood trembling.
He said to me, “Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day you set your heart on understanding and on standing before your God, your words were heard. I have come because of your words.
The ruler of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost princes, came to help me, and I remained there opposing the ruler of Persia.
I have come to show you what will happen to your people in the last days, for the vision still concerns the end of days.”
As he spoke these words to me, I lowered my face to the ground and remained silent.

Then someone with a human likeness touched my lips and opened my mouth. I spoke and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision my insides were in turmoil, and I could not stand.
How can this servant of my lord speak with my lord here? For I have no strength, and no breath remains in me.”
Again, the one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me.

He said to me, “Do not be afraid, greatly beloved man. Peace be with you. Be strong and take courage.” As he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and I said, “Let my lord speak, for I have been strengthened.”
He said to me, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight against the ruler of Persia. When I go out, the ruler of the Greeks will come.
But I will show you what is recorded in the book of truth. There is no one helping me in all these things except Michael, your ruler.
And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, he stood up to strengthen and support me.

Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and a fourth will gain far greater wealth than all of them. When he has become strong in his land, he will stir up all the kingdoms of the Greeks.
A mighty king will arise and rule with great authority, doing as he pleases.

When he has risen, his kingdom will be broken and scattered to the four winds of heaven. It will not be as it was for his posterity, nor will it have the authority with which he ruled. Rather, his kingdom will be uprooted, and there will be no others besides these.
The king of the south and his princes will grow strong, and one will become stronger than he and rule with great authority.

After some years they will come to an agreement. The daughter of the king of the south will go to the king of the north to make peace between them. But she will have no strength because of the fear that will seize her. She will be handed over, together with those who brought her, her young women, and those who supported her at that time.
Someone from the root of his offspring will arise in his place. He will come with an army and advance in strength against the king of the north. He will pass through them and prevail.
He will also carry down to Egypt their objects of worship, their precious vessels of silver and gold, and captives. He himself will stand against the king of the north for one or two years.
He will enter the stronghold of the king of the south and return to his own land.
His sons will wage war and gather large armies. They will advance against him, sweep through like a flood, and pass on. They will return and wage war as far as the stronghold.
The king of the south will become enraged and go out to confront the king of the north. He will raise a great army, but that army will be handed over to him.
He will destroy the army, and his heart will become proud. He will bring down many, but he will not grow strong.
The king of the north will return and raise an army larger than the first. At the end of one or two periods of time, he will come with a large army and powerful cavalry.
At that time many will rise against the king of the north. Wicked men among your people will rise up to fulfill the vision, but they will be overthrown.

The king of the north will come, set ambushes, and capture strong fortresses. The forces of the south will not stand, because they have no strength to stand. The chosen men of the people will take their stand, but they will not succeed, because they have no strength to stand.
The one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him. He will take his stand in the land of Israel, and it will be handed over to him.

He will set his face toward entering with the strength of all the kingdoms, and all his people will cross over. A woman will be given to him to bring about his destruction, but she will not stand firm or belong to him.
He will turn his face toward the islands of the sea and conquer many. He will put an end to the ruler who was insulting him and turn his insult back on him.
He will turn his face toward the stronghold of the land, but he will be overthrown and fall, and he will not be found.
In his place will arise one who takes away power and the splendor of kings. Within a few days he will be broken, neither through anger nor in battle.
In his place a weak man will arise. Royal splendor will not be bestowed on him, but he will come quietly and seize the kingdom through deceit.
The strength of the fortified cities will be plundered, and they will be broken before him, as will the leaders of the covenant.
Those who ally themselves with him will plot against him. He will rise and grow strong with a small people.

And in the richest parts of the cities, he will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will carry off plunder, captives, and their possessions. He will devise plans against their fortified cities, but only for a time.

He will rouse his strength and courage against the king of the south with a large and powerful army. The king of the south will be stirred to battle with a large army and will become exceedingly strong, but he will not stand, because plots will be devised against him.
Those who eat his royal food will break him. His army will be scattered, and many will fall slain.
Both these kings will have their hearts set on evil. They will speak deceitfully at one table, but they will not succeed, because the end comes at its appointed time.
He will return to his land with a large army. His heart will be set against the holy covenant, and he will act.
As at the beginning, so also at the end.
The armies of Kittim will come against him and break him. He will return and rage against the holy covenant, and he will give attention to those who have abandoned the holy covenant.
Their forces will arise from among them. They will defile the mighty sanctuary, remove the offerings, and set up a defilement that brings destruction.
He will condemn those who transgress the covenant, but the people who know the faith will grow strong.
The righteous among the people will teach many, but they will fall by the sword, by fire, through captivity, and through plunder, for a thousand days.
When they are overthrown, they will receive a little help, and many will join them with divided loyalty.
Some of the wise will be overthrown, to test them and bring understanding, until the time of the end, because there is still a delay before the appointed time.

The king will do as he pleases and exalt himself above every god. He will speak boastful things against the God of gods, and he will prosper until the wrath is finished, because what was decreed has been done.
He will pay no attention to the God of his fathers. He will have no regard for the desire of women or for any god, but will exalt himself above everything.
In his place he will honor a mighty god. He will honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and desirable things.
He will enter strong fortresses with foreign gods whom he recognizes. He will rule over many and divide the land for a price.
At the time of the end, the king of the south will fight against him. The king of the north will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships, and will enter the land.
He will reach the land of Israel, and many will be killed. But these will escape from his hands: Edom, Moab, and the rest of the Ammonites.
He will stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape his hands.
He will control the treasury of gold and silver and all the precious things of Egypt. The Libyans and Cushites will be his helpers.
Reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out in great fury to devastate and destroy many.
He will pitch his tent in a pleasant place between the sea and the mountain, and guard his sanctuary. The time of his end will come, and he will have no helper.

At that time Michael, the great angel appointed over your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress unlike any since ancient times. At that time, everyone among your people who is found written in the book will be delivered.
Many of those who sleep in the dust will awake: some to everlasting life, and others to destruction and the everlasting contempt of their companions.
Those who do good and those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the sky. Those who lead many to righteousness will shine and endure like the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, seal up these words and be silent. Seal this book until the time of the end. Many will search, and knowledge will increase.
I, Daniel, looked, and there were two others standing there, one on this bank of the river and one on the other.
They said to the man dressed in splendid clothing, who stood above the waters of the river, “How long until this end?”

I heard the man dressed in splendid garments, who stood above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the hands of all the holy people are freed, all these things will be completed.
I, Daniel, heard but did not understand. I said, “My lord, what comes after these things?”
He said to me, “Go, Daniel, for the words are hidden and sealed until the time of the end.
Many will be chosen, made white, and tested. Sinners will sin, and none of the sinners will understand, but those who do good will understand.
From the time the offering is removed and the abomination is set up to bring destruction, there will be 1,290 days.
Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.
But you, Daniel, go to the end. Rest, and you will arise at your appointed time, at the end of the days.”
